enAudit: NEW — G1-270: the instruction "Double the group, then halve it. Small numbers to start." describes a two-step operation on one group, but the render is four INDEPENDENT cards, each carrying its own label (double / half) and its own different set of foxes (3+3, half of 6, 2+2, half of 2). The child never halves a group they doubled. This is a flow the page does not have; the honest sentence is "read the label on each card: double or half".

NEW — K-299: the title "Copy the Picture Using Letters and Numbers" names a property it SHARES with K-300, which is also labelled (A-H / 1-8). Same defect class as the already-fixed G1-263. Against K-298 the true delta is the labels; against K-300 it is the smaller 6x6 grid, and only one of those is in the title.

NEW — G1-258 / G1-259: the same shared-property class again. "With a Word Bank" and "Choose from the Word Bank" both name the bank, which BOTH pages have (bank:true). The real delta is starter:true — G1-258 prints the first letter of every word and G1-259 does not. The instructions do carry it; the titles do not, so the two pages are indistinguishable in a SERP.

NEW — G2-294: every card on this page is a canBuy, and in two independently seeded renders ALL THREE answers were "no" (45 vs 35+15=50, 40 vs 35+30=65, 50 vs 40+35=75). A three-card yes/no page whose answers are identical can be completed correctly by writing one word three times, with no arithmetic. The generator needs a mixed-verdict constraint, the way the sum-ceiling checks constrain the number ranges.

NEW — G2-285: the instruction never mentions that some word chips carry a supporting picture (pics:true — dolphin, seagull, giraffe are illustrated). That picture support is the ONLY thing separating this face from G2-286, whose instruction DOES say "No pictures to help". The contrast is stated on one side of the pair only, so G2-285 reads as the generic face of the family.

NEW — G1-268: "A bottom brick is missing. Use the brick above to find it." describes only the one missing bottom brick, but every other brick in all four walls is also empty and has to be built. The instruction under-describes the task a child actually faces; "then build the rest of the wall" is missing.

NEW — G1-256: the number of the day is drawn from 11-19, so "ten more" is always 21-29 — OUTSIDE the 0-20 number line printed on the same page (line.max = 20). Not wrong, but the page supplies a number line that cannot be used to check the very answer the page asks for. Either the line should run to 30 or the ten-more box belongs on the up-to-99 face.

NEW — G2-300: the title "Your Own Words" and the instruction "No sentence starters" overclaim. A word bank of six labelled nouns is still printed on the page (nouns:6). The real delta against G2-299 is the absence of the sentence starters (starters:null), not the absence of supplied vocabulary. "No sentence starters this time" alone would be honest; "your own words" is not.

NEW — G2-293: beyond the duplicated card already reported, EVERY card on the page is paid with the same two 25c coins, so the tendered amount is 50 on all three. "Count the coins paid" is therefore never a real sub-task — the child counts the identical pair three times. Also card 1 asks "How much money does Mia get back?" while cards 2 and 3 ask "How much change does X get?" — two registers for one question type on one page.

KNOWN (seen, corroborating) — G1-264: "Two words start alike" over a page of SIX words in TWO pairs (baby/boat and scooter/swing). Both pairs need the second letter; the singular framing describes one.

KNOWN (seen, corroborating) — G2-281: the same names-need-capitals gap that was fixed in G2-282. Two of the four sentences begin with a lowercase proper name ("anna has a big fox", "ben likes the little donkey"), but needCaps is 0, the legend carries only "Capital letter" and "End mark", and the instruction says only "a capital letter and a full stop". A child who capitalises just the first word has not finished the sentence.

KNOWN (seen, corroborating) — the G3 grouping stories state the arrangement as already done while the strip is drawn ungrouped, in rows of ten: G3-373 ("Ben makes groups of 5" over a flat strip), G3-374 card 2 ("arranges 10 cranberries in rows of 5" drawn as one row of 10), G3-375 card 2 ("20 koalas in rows of 5" drawn as 2 rows of 10) and G3-376 card 3. The rows-of-ten layout is deliberate (it must not restate the quotient), so the fix belongs in the story wording, not the picture.

DATA (fixed by the regeneration, recorded) — the first out/b2var-faces.json I read carried three stale themes (G1-283, G3-372, G3-376 all said vehicles) and a sweep path g1283-vehicles.png that did not exist on disk, while loadType(id).i18n.en already held the corrected English. The generator, not the exported table, is the source of truth; a panel briefed only from the table would have named three themes wrongly.

NEW — G2-306: "Find both capitals, not just the first" is false on the page that ships. ends:["."] drops every question frame, and all nine surviving {name} frames in the it bank put the name FIRST ("{name} vede tre {noun}.", "{name} conta cinque {noun}.", "{name} ha sei {noun}." …), so the name IS the opening word and there is exactly ONE capital to restore. Only two of the sixteen frames carry a second {name} mid-sentence and neither is guaranteed to be drawn. Measured on the render: "giulia ha sei ippopotami" / "giulia disegna quattro gufi" / "aurora conta cinque elefanti" — three lines, three single capitals. Honest English: "Every sentence names somebody: the capital is a name, not just a sentence opener." The sentence-initial-{name} shape is not an Italian accident — check the other ten banks.

NEW — G2-306, second defect on the same render: the same name is drawn twice on a three-line page (giulia, giulia, aurora). rng.sample(bank.names, 2) runs per lane with no cross-lane exclusion, so on a face whose whole subject is proper names two thirds of it can carry one name. The it bank has eight names; a per-page distinct-name constraint belongs next to the existing needCaps guard.

NEW — G1-284: "some letters sit right next to each other" states as fact what the config only permits. d2 sets gap:1, which requires the six first letters to be DISTINCT; nothing asserts a single adjacent pair (this seed happened to give a-b-c, the next need not). The honest form is "may be". Also the real d1→d2 delta is gap 3→1 as much as 4→6 cards, and the English title names only the count.

NEW — K-312: "Longer words than the first page" points at a page the child does not have. A printable is downloaded on its own, so "the first page" names nothing — the same class as the removed "the previous sheet" wording.

NEW — K-308 / G1-285 / G2-304 all inherit d1 (window:10, count:20), so only TEN dots are numbered and the rest of the outline is already printed — confirmed on the K-308 render (labels 10→1, grey pre-printed remainder). None of the three English instructions says so, while their d1 sibling K-294 does ("to finish the picture"). A child who counts 10, 9, 8 … 1 and stops has not finished the drawing. G1-294 (window:null) is the one face of the four where the numbers run the whole way, and the only one whose English gets it right.

NEW — five of these thirteen faces are param-identical to their own base: K-312, G1-284, G1-290, G2-309 and G3-377 each spread base.difficulty[2] with an EMPTY override while the waves ship difficulties:[2], so the rendered page is the base's shipped page with a different theme and seed. Their titles distinguish them from their SIBLINGS but not from the base they duplicate — K-284 "Trace and Write the Words" already IS the ≤9-letter page, G1-245 "ABC Order" already IS six words. This is the K-299 / G1-258-259 shared-property defect one level up: a title promising a distinction the base already owns.

NEW — K-311: the English is right about the mechanics and wrong about the family. With traceLane:false there is no dashed lane anywhere (render: gabbiano / pesce / elefante / delfino printed solid on the card, two empty rails each), so the family verb "Trace" does not apply to this face. Rule 5 (inherit the genre head) and rule 4 (honesty) collide here; Italian renamed it (Ricopia…) rather than inherit Ricalca. Flagged so the other ten panels are not marked down for the same call.

BUILD — G2-309 cannot ship in Italian on its pinned theme. MEASURED: wsg-wb2varit-g2309-vehicles-d2-it fails the QA overflow lint (four divs and an svg past the page box) on every attempt — with an 87-char instruction, with a 43-char one, and with a 6-char title plus a 9-char instruction, so it is NOT the header copy. The same face builds clean on it+animals, it+toys and it+fruits, and on de/es/nl/fi + vehicles. The base G2-278 vehicles/d2/it shipped, so it is seed-dependent, not config-dependent. Italian needs an EXCEPT.it['G2-309'] theme alongside the K-306/K-307 exceptions, or the picture-writing d2 stack must absorb a taller Italian word bank. Its Italian copy is written and gate-clean but is the one pair not confirmed against a render or a real meta description.

DATA — out/b2var-faces.json still holds only the first 64 faces: none of the sixteen wave-2 ids is in it and out/b2var-sweep/ has no renders for them, so a panel following the brief literally ("the exact path is in the sweep field") would have had nothing to look at. I built the wave instead (cli.js generate --wave waves/wave-b2var-it.json --types=…) and read the thumbnails out of the staged ZIPs; that should be the brief's wave-2 instruction.

MEASURED — the Italian description budget is about half the Spanish figure the brief quotes. The it lead is "Scheda stampabile gratis: <TITLE> Scheda di esercizi (<Tema>) per <Livello>." plus " Scarica il PDF gratis.", costing 84-103 chars BEFORE the title, so the JOINT budget is titleLen + instructionLen ≤ 84 themeless and ≤ 65-69 themed. All thirteen instructions are 24-47 chars. On eight of the thirteen the it core already exceeds 120 with no middle at all, so the floor never binds and only the 170 ceiling does; the exceptions are G1-284 and the two write-the-word faces, where the family skill sentence does band and must also be beaten — G1-291 needed its title cut from 33 to 26 chars to open a window at all.
